'''''Melaleuca glauca''''', commonly known as '''Albany bottlebrush''' is a plant in the myrtle [[Family (taxonomy)|family]], [[Myrtaceae]] and is [[Endemism|endemic]] to the [[Southwest Australia|south-west]] of [[Western Australia]]. (Some Australian state [[Herbarium|herbaria]] continue to use the name ''Callistemon glaucus''. [[Lyndley Craven]] claims that there is no [[Type (biology)|type material]] for ''Callistemon speciosus'' and includes it here as a synonym.)<ref name=Udovicic>{{cite journal|last1=Udovicic|first1=Frank|last2=Spencer|first2=Roger|title=New combinations in ''Callistemon'' (Myrtaceae)|journal=Muelleria|date=2012|volume=30|issue=1|pages=23–25|doi=10.5962/p.292240 |s2cid=251007557 |url=http://www.rbg.vic.gov.au/documents/Muelleria_30-1_3_Udovicic_Spencer.pdf|accessdate=11 June 2015}}</ref><ref name=APC>{{cite web |title=''Callistemon speciosus'' (Sims) Colvill ex Sweet |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/search?product=apc&tree.id=1133571&name=Callistemon+speciosus&max=100&display=apc&search=true |publisher=Australian Plant Census |accessdate=22 July 2015}}</ref> It is a tall shrub with [[glaucous]] leaves and spikes of red flowers in spring.

==Description==
''Melaleuca glauca'' is a shrub growing to {{convert|3.5|m|ft|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} tall with hard, fibrous bark. Its leaves are arranged alternately and are {{convert|40-128|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long, {{convert|3-18|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide, flat, mostly narrow egg-shaped with a mid-vein and 11 to 20 branching veins.<ref name=Brophy>{{cite book|last1=Brophy|first1=Joseph J.|last2=Craven|first2=Lyndley A.|last3=Doran|first3=John C.|title=Melaleucas : their botany, essential oils and uses|date=2013|publisher=Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research|location=Canberra|isbn=9781922137517|pages=177–178}}</ref>

The flowers are bright red and arranged in spikes on the ends of branches which continue to grow after flowering. The spikes are up to {{convert|75|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} in diameter with 20 to 120 or more individual flowers. The petals are {{convert|4.5-7.2|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long and fall off as the flower ages. The stamens are arranged in five bundles around the flower and there are between 6 and 15 stamens per bundle. Flowering occurs from October to December and is followed by fruit which are woody [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]]s, {{convert|5.7-8.8|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long.<ref name=Brophy/>
[[File:Melaleuca glauca (leaves, flowers, fruits).JPG|thumb|Habit in [[Gull Rock National Park]]]]

==Taxonomy and naming==
The Albany bottlebrush was first formally described in 1830 by the [[English people|English]] botanist [[Robert Sweet (botanist)|Robert Sweet]], who gave it the name ''Callistemon glaucus'' and published the description in his book ''Hortus Britannicus''.<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Melaleuca glauca''|url= https://biodiversity.org.au/boa/instance/apni/773227|publisher=APNI|accessdate=5 August 2015}}</ref><ref name=Sweet>{{cite book|last1=Sweet|first1=Robert|title=Hortus Britannicus|date=1830|publisher=James Ridgway|location=London|page=209|edition=2nd|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/41438#page/224/mode/1up|accessdate=13 July 2015}}</ref> In 2013, [[Lyndley Craven]] changed the name to ''Melaleuca glauca'' and published the name change in ''Melaleucas : their botany, essential oils and uses''.<ref name=Brophy/>

In 1815 [[Aimé Bonpland]] described ''Metrosideros glauca'' but the name was not a validly published name (a [[nomen illegitimum|nom. illeg.]]),<ref name="WCSP3">{{cite web |url=http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=126421 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014181540/https://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=126421 |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 October 2022 |title=''Metrosideros glauca'' |work=[[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] (WCSP) |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] }}</ref> having already been used by [[Georges Louis Marie Dumont de Courset|Georges de Courset]] in 1811.<ref name="WCSP2">{{cite web |url=http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=126420 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015175602/https://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=126420 |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 October 2022 |title=''Metrosideros glauca'' |work=[[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] (WCSP) |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] }}</ref> ''Callistemon glaucus'' is regarded as a synonym of ''Melaleuca glauca'' by the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]].<ref name ="WCSP1">{{cite web |url=http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=31430 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302233248/http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=31430 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 March 2021 |title=''Callistemon glaucus'' |work=[[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] (WCSP) |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] }}</ref>

The [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] (''glauca'') is from the [[Latin]] ''glaucus'' meaning "[[wikt:glaucous|glaucous]]", referring to the leaves seen by Bonpland.<ref name="Brophy" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Melaleuca glauca'' occurs in the south and south-western coastal districts of Western Australia between [[Perth, Western Australia|Perth]] and [[Albany, Western Australia|Albany]] in the [[Jarrah Forest]], [[Swan Coastal Plain]] and [[Warren (biogeographic region)|Warren]] [[IBRA|biogeographic regions]], where it grows in swampy ground in sandy or clayey soils.<ref name="Brophy" /><ref name=flora>{{cite book|last1=Paczkowska|first1=Grazyna|last2=Chapman|first2=Alex R.|title=The Western Australian flora : a descriptive catalogue|date=2000|publisher=Wildflower Society of Western Australia|location=Perth|isbn=0646402439|page=350}}</ref><ref name=FloraBase>{{FloraBase|name=''Melaleuca glauca''|id = 5394}}</ref>

==Conservation status==
''Melaleuca glauca'' is listed as not threatened by the [[Government of Western Australia]] [[Department of Parks and Wildlife (Western Australia)|Department of Parks and Wildlife]].<ref name="FloraBase" />

==Use in horticulture==
''Melaleuca glauca'' is widely grown as an ornamental (as ''Callistemon glaucus'') in temperate parts of Australia.<ref name="Brophy" />
